column1: # ---- 03-contracts/C6 ----
C6 carries the StateSnapshot payload at version 1.0 from L0 to L1, L2 and L3, and is the read side of L0.
C6 is the contract the state store was asserted to be, with a field table, a version and invariants like every other seam.
C6 is numbered separately from C5 rather than folded into it because it has a different direction, a different set of consumers and a different failure policy.
The StateSnapshot is taken once, immutably, at the top of every tick, and every layer that needs state reads that one object.
No layer consults L0 directly mid-tick, which is what makes the no-read-of-a-same-tick-write audit mechanically decidable.

StateUpdate and StateSnapshot are deliberately not the same type: the snapshot is a coherent read view of the whole store at an instant, and the update is a delta produced by one component at the end of a tick.
snapshotAt is the tick at which the snapshot was taken.
stateAsOf is the latest tick whose StateUpdate is included and is always strictly less than snapshotAt.
lagSlots equals snapshotAt minus stateAsOf and is the explicit feedback lag.
isColdStart is true on the first tick after a restart, before reconciliation completes.
lagSlots is a first-class field rather than an implementation detail, and consumers are expected to reason about it.
A Planner that knows the peak state is three slots stale treats the gap conservatively rather than assuming it was empty.
The C6 peak state block mirrors C5 §2 and is read by PeakView in L2 and by the escalation policy in L3.
realisedPeak on C6 is the EpigraphTerm floor.
peakIsProvisional defaults to true.
The peak is authoritative only up to unsettledGapFrom.
The conservative default for headroomToPeakKw is zero, meaning no headroom.
The conservative default for peakCritical is true, meaning treat the state as critical.
The unsettled gap is not optional to handle.
Between unsettledGapFrom and snapshotAt no settled meter data exists.
The Planner must substitute its own modelled POI trajectory over the unsettled window as a provisional peak contribution.
effectiveFloor is the maximum of realisedPeak and the maximum modelled POI import over the slots in [unsettledGapFrom, snapshotAt).
Assuming the unsettled gap contained nothing is the single most likely way to set a new monthly peak by accident, because the gap is exactly the window in which the engine was most recently active.
The C6 qualification state block mirrors C5 §3 and is read by TariffView and PeakView in L2 and by the slow loop.
fullLoadHours is a declared exception to the dimensionless rule, carrying the declared unit h.
The conservative default for qualificationStatus is AtRisk.
The conservative default for qualificationMarginHours is zero, meaning no margin.
The conservative default for qualCritical is true.

Every conservative default in the qualification block biases toward protecting the qualification, because the asymmetry is extreme: the downside of an unnecessary protective bound is a day's foregone spread while the downside of losing a §19(2) reduction is a year of network-charge relief.
The C6 delineation state block mirrors C5 §3.1 and is read by DelineationView in L2 and by L3, which carries the accumulators forward as MILP variables over the horizon.
The seven accumulators cross C6 unchanged from C5 §3.1, defaulting to zero.
The conservative defaults for pvShare and awPositiveShare are zero, meaning no PV attribution and no AW>0 share.
A false throughputBoundMet forces the Planner to carry (12) explicitly rather than assume it away.

The delineation conservative defaults bias toward understating delineation value: a zero awPositiveShare prices the green route at nothing, and throughputBoundMet = false costs binaries rather than correctness.
The failure mode worth avoiding is an engine that charges from the grid on the strength of a route it turns out not to have.
DelineationView reads the C6 delineation block and the MW_month belief and publishes the seven λ_j, and it reads no other view's output.
The commitment ledger read view mirrors C5 §4 and is read by L3.
Ledger entries are ordered by (slot, entryId) for determinism.
confirmedReserveUp and confirmedReserveDn are denormalised per block for the Planner's hard constraints.
confirmedSpotPosition is denormalised, signed, and in the market frame.
pendingExposure is signed and probabilistic rather than an obligation.
requiredSocCorridor is the union of all confirmed feasibilityRequirements.
A false ledgerConsistent triggers SAFE mode.
The denormalised ledger views exist because the Planner needs them on every solve, and recomputing them from entries per tick is both wasteful and a chance to disagree.
requiredSocCorridor is the single most safety-critical field in C6.
requiredSocCorridor is a hard constraint in every degradation mode including SAFE, and a plan that violates it never reaches C3.
The value function is read from C6 by OppCostView in L2, which republishes it across C2 §4.
isStale is true when snapshotAt minus producedAt exceeds validityHorizon.
contextDrift is the distance from the state at which V was fitted.
Value function staleness is never silent.
If the value function is stale the mode escalates to at least DEFENSIVE and stalenessPenalty shrinks V's slopes toward zero.
Shrinking V's slopes toward zero makes the Planner progressively indifferent to terminal SOC rather than confidently wrong about it.
T6 includes a stale-artefact audit asserting the engine refuses a value function beyond its validity horizon rather than using it quietly.
degradationMode on C6 is the mode in force entering the tick.
modeEnteredAt is carried for hysteresis accounting.
consecutiveBadTicks and consecutiveGoodTicks are the hysteresis counters.
seriesQualityState carries the last known QualityStamp per series.
The mode in the snapshot is a floor and not a verdict.
L1 may raise the degradation mode within the tick from its own same-tick inputs but may never lower it.
A critical series missing now escalates now and does not wait a tick.
De-escalation of the degradation mode is central and hysteretic.
Raising a floor from a component's own inputs is not a read of another component's same-tick write, so in-tick escalation does not violate ADR-006.
artefactVersions maps each ArtefactKind — scenario generator, value function, fill model, tier-3 surface, market calendar, tzdata — to a content hash.
artefactVersions is carried so that every downstream artefact can record which model versions produced it and so a backtest can be re-run with the versions actually in force.
Denormalised ledger views reconcile with entries, and violation is a HALT.
stateAsOf is strictly less than snapshotAt and lagSlots is consistent with both, and violation is a HALT because a zero lag means a same-tick read.
The snapshot is immutable for the duration of the tick and no consumer holds a mutable reference, enforced structurally and audited in T3.
Every C6 field marked Null = no is present, or the default is applied and recorded, and otherwise the engine escalates.
requiredSocCorridor is non-empty wherever confirmedReserveUp or confirmedReserveDn is non-zero, and violation is a HALT.
On isColdStart no speculative intent is emitted until reconciliation completes, and violation is a HALT.

The lag invariant is the mechanical enforcement of ADR-006, because a lag of zero would mean some component read state written in the same tick, which is precisely the cycle the architecture exists to exclude.
No belief or forecast crosses C6, because those come from L1 via C1.
No valuation output crosses C6: L0 stores V as an artefact and does not store prices.
No raw settlement detail crosses C6; only the aggregated state the next tick needs.
No mutable references to the store cross C6, because the snapshot is a value.
